item.title: NCUA Launches Deregulation Project and Proposes Four Rules to Streamline Credit Union Regulations
item.description: On December 10, 2025, the National Credit Union Administration announced a new Deregulation Project and issued the first package of proposed rules aimed at streamlining its regulatory framework for federally insured credit unions under the Federal Credit Union Act. item.title: CFPB Finalizes 2026 Increase to Fair Credit Reporting Act Disclosure Fee Cap
item.description: On December 15, the CFPB issued a final rule amending Regulation V under the Fair Credit Reporting Act to update the maximum amount a consumer reporting agency may charge a consumer for certain file disclosures. The amendment implements FCRA’s annual inflation adjustment requirement and sets the ceiling for calendar year 2026. item.title: California Broadly Interprets “Doing Business” for LLC Tax, Finding Nexus Thresholds Are Not a Safe Harbor
item.description: In a recent case focusing on statutory interpretation, the California Office of Tax Appeals (“OTA”) held that a Delaware LLC using Amazon’s Fulfillment by Amazon (“FBA”) program was “doing business” in California and subject to the state’s annual $800 LLC tax. item.title: CFPB and Federal Reserve Finalize 2026 Inflation Adjustments to Consumer Leasing and Truth in Lending Coverage Thresholds
item.description: On December 15, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and the CFPB issued joint final rules amending the official interpretations to their regulations implementing the Consumer Leasing Act and the Truth in Lending Act. The amendments reflect the annual inflation adjustment required by statute and increase the exemption thresholds effective January 1, 2026. item.title: EU’s Omnibus I Package - Major Changes to Corporate Sustainability Reporting and Due Diligence – What Multinationals Need to Know
item.description: December 2025 has brought a pivotal shakeup in European sustainability regulations. item.title: New York Legislature Amends CPLR 2106 To Resolve Lingering Confusion over Affirmation Use
item.description: On November 21, 2025, New York State Governor Kathy Hochul signed into law Senate Bill S8195, ushering in a significant clarification to CPLR 2106, which authorizes the use of unsworn (i.e., not notarized) affirmations in civil actions, akin to declarations in the federal system under 28 U.S.C. § 1746.
